text:
Alex: quick heads-up — I noticed our KV eviction metric looks flat but memory growth keeps climbing on long-context traces. think we have mismatched signals between eviction_count, residency, and reuse.
Maya: can you paste the queries/trace you used? :eyes:
Alex: sure — here's what I pulled from prod prometheus this morning:
```
# eviction rate per shard (5m)
sum by (shard) (increase(kv_evictions_total[5m]))

# global residency ratio (approx)
(sum(kv_resident_entries_total) / sum(kv_entries_expected_total)) * 100
```
Result: eviction rate low but resident_entries_total keeps increasing over 6h on a few hosts.
Rishi: that smells like fragmentation + reuse mismatch. If fragments are small but numerous, residency can climb even if eviction_count is low because we aren't coalescing slots.
Jen: do we have eviction_age buckets? eviction_time_seconds_bucket or something? that would show how long items live before eviction.
Alex: we have kv_eviction_age_seconds_bucket but it's not exposed in the current dashboard. here's a sample query I hacked:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_eviction_age_seconds_bucket[1h])) by (le, model))
```
Maya: nice — we should show p50/p95/p99 for eviction_age and residency. Also add per-model and per-shard breakdowns.
Rishi: +1. Also suggest a reuse metric: fraction of cache hits that used an existing fragment vs reloaded fragment. we can approximate via labels: kv_hit_total{reuse="true"} / kv_hit_total
Jen: the tricky bit: our sampling skews long sessions. long-context sessions add more resident entries; eviction_count per-second might stay low but per-session eviction probability is high. we should weight by active_sessions or show per-session residency quantiles.
Alex: agreed. proposal: unify signals into a small panel set and an alert runbook. panels:
- KV: eviction rate (1m/5m/1h) by shard + model :bar_chart:
- KV: residency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) by model :chart_with_upwards_trend:
- KV: eviction_age histogram (p50/p95/p99) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- KV: reuse_ratio heatmap (model x shard) — show low reuse hotspots
- KV: per-request hit_rate and per-session residency distribution
- Sampling bias note and link to sampler notebook
Maya: for alerts, what thresholds? current infra-bot fired a few times last week with no follow-up.
infra-bot: alert: kv_evictions_total increased 2.4x on host gpu-12 in the last 30m. incident: none. :warning:
Rishi: threshold idea: alert when eviction_rate (5m) > baseline_rolling_mean(1d) * 3 AND eviction_age_p95 > X ms. baseline_rolling_mean can be computed with recording rules.
Jen: also have a soft alert for residency growth slope: if residency_p50 slopes up > 10% over 1h for a model, page on-call. that catches slow drift.
Maya: I can prototype a Grafana folder and panel JSON to share. will wire queries + templates (model, shard). will also add link to sampler notebook so SREs can reproduce.
Alex: action items:
- Maya: create dashboard PR + templates (ETA EOD Tue)
- Rishi: add reuse_ratio and eviction_age recording rules + example queries (ETA tomorrow)
- Jen: update alerts and write short runbook snippet for what to check (sampling, fragmentation, model rollout) (ETA Thu)
- Alex: follow up with perf team to see if kernel selection/batching changes correlate with the time window where residency started climbing.
Maya: tagging @oncall to review once dashboard is up. :thumbsup:
Jen: thanks — will start drafting runbook steps (how to compute per-session residency, how to force eviction sampling).
Alex: awesome. if anyone has more concrete examples of long-context traces that show growth, drop them here or link to the sampler notebook.
Maya: I'll attach a small synthetic trace in the PR to demonstrate the skew.
Rishi: FYI I already added a recording rule draft in my branch: `kv:eviction_rate:5m` and `kv:residency_quantiles:1h` — will push today.
Alex: perfect. re-checking later this afternoon. :eyes:
